Structure and mechanics:

Good practices (industry):
Thermal:
• Thermal budget calculated or simulated, junction temperature at least # °C below the component maximum
• Touched-surface temperature per IEC #-# (TS#) or IEC #-#, with margin
• Materials chosen with a thermal index (RTI, UL #B) above the temperature reached
• Thermal protection (thermistor, thermal cut-out) that puts the product in a safe state
• Assured, repeatable thermal contact: specified paste or pad, tightening torque, flatness
• Temperature derating of components (manufacturer's curve)
EMC and radio:
• Continuous ground plane, short current loops, written placement and routing rules
• Filtering at the power input (ferrite, X / Y capacitors) and on every cable leaving the enclosure
• ESD protection (TVS) on every touched surface and accessible connector (IEC #-#-#)
• Pre-certified ISED / FCC radio module with the antenna and placement from its integration sheet
• Switching frequency outside sensitive bands, softened edges or spread spectrum
Electronics and software:
• Watchdog and a defined safe state at startup, on fault and on power loss
• IEC #-# Annex H (Class B) if the software performs a safety function
• Coding rules (e.g. MISRA C), code review and static analysis before each release
• Automated unit and integration tests, rerun on every change
• Input validation, timeouts and automatic communication recovery
• Non-volatile memory protected by CRC, writes limited to the memory endurance
• Signed update with the possibility to roll back to the previous version
• Sensors: filtering and debouncing, thresholds with hysteresis, measurement plausibility checks
For any function:
• Purchased part: datasheet read in full, qualified supplier, second source identified
• Peer design review (PDR, CDR) with this DFMEA line in front of the reviewers
• Lessons learned: DFMEA and field feedback from a similar or previous product
• Proven solution or qualified off-the-shelf part rather than a new technology, unless there is a quantified reason
• Quantified, verifiable requirement in the functional specification (CdCF) (Goldmine) for this function, with its tolerance

Good practices (industry):
Electronics and software:
• Watchdog and a defined safe state at startup, on fault and on power loss
• IEC #-# Annex H (Class B) if the software performs a safety function
• Coding rules (e.g. MISRA C), code review and static analysis before each release
• Automated unit and integration tests, rerun on every change
• Input validation, timeouts and automatic communication recovery
• Non-volatile memory protected by CRC, writes limited to the memory endurance
• Signed update with the possibility to roll back to the previous version
• Sensors: filtering and debouncing, thresholds with hysteresis, measurement plausibility checks
Moving parts and lifetime:
• Lifetime specified in cycles, with a margin of at least # times the intended use
• Materials paired against wear (plastic on metal, specified lubricant), no two identical plastics rubbing together
• Switches and buttons chosen for a known number of cycles (datasheet), with debouncing
• Adjustable friction or clamping, wear take-up provided
• No finger pinching or shearing by moving parts (IEC #-#, cl. #)
For any function:
• Peer design review (PDR, CDR) with this DFMEA line in front of the reviewers
• Lessons learned: DFMEA and field feedback from a similar or previous product
• Proven solution or qualified off-the-shelf part rather than a new technology, unless there is a quantified reason
• Quantified, verifiable requirement in the functional specification (CdCF) (Goldmine) for this function, with its tolerance

Electronics and software:
• Watchdog and a defined safe state at startup, on fault and on power loss
• IEC #-# Annex H (Class B) if the software performs a safety function

• Automated unit and integration tests, rerun on every change
• Input validation, timeouts and automatic recovery of communications
• Non-volatile memory protected by CRC, writes limited to the memory's endurance
• Signed update with the ability to roll back to the previous version
• Sensors: filtering and debouncing, thresholds with hysteresis, measurement plausibility checks
Electrical safety:
• Air clearances and surface distances per IEC #-# or IEC #-#, for the working voltage and pollution degree
• Double or reinforced insulation between the mains and accessible parts (Class II), or verified grounding (Class I)
• Certified external CSA / UL power supply (Class #, ES# / PS#) rather than a built-in mains supply
• Overcurrent protection (fuse, PTC) sized for the fault current
• Component derating: voltage ≤ #%, current ≤ #-#%, power ≤ #-#% of the rated value
• List of safety-critical components, each certified and frozen (no replacement without review)
• Single fault analysis: one shorted or open component does not make the product hazardous

• Peer design review (PDR, CDR) with this DFMEA line in front of the reviewers
• Lessons learned: DFMEA and field feedback from a similar or previous product
